sources.title: Ford and Fulkerson, Maximal Flow Through a Network (1956)
sources.complete: Six scanned original pages399–404, including all3sections, proofs, both figures, footnotes and references. Read complete serialOCR, visually inspected all6pages. OMP_THREAD_LIMIT=1.

anchors.claim: Finite undirected network with positive capacities; flow defined as nonnegative simple-chain collection. Introduction explicitly calls general proof nonconstructive. Theorem1 proves maximal flow=minimal disconnecting-set capacity. Compact chain-flow polytope gives existence; averaging maximalflows gives Lemma1; orientation/cancellation and leftarcs give Lemmas2–3 and exact cut equality.

Corollary: adding/subtracting equal capacity on an arcset meeting every cut once shifts networkcapacity equally. §2 requires source–sink planarity; Theorem2 supplies a topmost/bottommost chain meeting every cut once. Saturate chain, subtract bottleneck, delete saturatedarcs, repeat. Atleastoneedge deleted per step gives finite termination. Fig1 shows failure for paired multicommodity demands; Fig2 shows the special chain property fails without terminal planarity.
§3 constructs shortest-path/mincut duality for source–sink-planar networks. No general directed residual-labeling algorithm or integral-capacity corollary is stated here.

anchors.claim: Jordanpolygon, open diagonal insidepolygon, disjoint earinteriors; all nontriangles have two nonoverlapping ears. Induct via removableconvexear, or select nearest parallel line through vertex in closed cornertriangle (including on opposite chord); split on VZ, select ears away from common endpoints. Figure1 illustrates split;2–4 show manyears, exactlytwoears and starshapedexample.

Repeated ear removal triangulates with no new vertices; conversely triangle boundary-edge counts yield t2=t0+2≥2. Angle sum yields n−2triangles; Euler gives n−3noncrossingdiagonals. These match the existing theorem/demo scope.
